Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

2. REQjUIREMENTS 

2.1 Descriptioa — The material ihall be smooth^ dark grey, 
homogeneous and free from grit or other visible impurities^ and shall not 
show any signs of breakdown, hardening or tendency of the constituents 
to separate. In addition, the material shall also be free from any 
objectionable odour. 

2J2 Composition — The material shall be prepared from the following 
ingredients in such proportions as to comply with the requirements 
prescribed in Table 1: 

a) Mitufol Lubricating Oil — The mineral lubricating oil extracted 
from the grease by Method *A* prescribed in P : 59 of 
IS : 1448* shall comply with the following requiremenu:

between the purchtser and the supplier. 

c) Graphite Flaki —6*10 percent by mass (conforming 16 IS : 495- 
1967t).

3. PACKING AND MARKING 

3.1 Packing — The material shall be packed ii\ suitable, clean, dry, 
leakproof containers free from rust, as agreed to between the purchaser 
and the supplier. 

3.2 Marldng — The containers shall be marked with the name of the 
material; net mass in the container; name of the manufacturer and 
recognized trade-mark, if any; batch number or code number; year and 
country of manufacture. 

3.3 BIS CertiflcalioB MhrUag 

The product may also be Riaifced with Standaid Maik. 

3.3.1 The use of the Standaid Mark is governed by the piovbtona of the 
Buitau of Indian Sundanb Act, 1986 and the Rules and RegulatkuM made 
theieunder. The detaib of oonditioBS under which the Noenoe for die use of 
Sundard Mark may be granted to manufactuiro or pioduceis may tie obtained 
from the Bureau of Indian Standards* 



4. SAMPLING 

4.1 Representative samples of the material shall be drawn as prescribed 
in IS : 1447.1966*. 

4.2 Criteria for Conformity — Tests for consistency and resistance to 
breakdown shall be done in individual samples and other t^sts on 
composite sample. The lot shall be declared satisfactory only if all 
individual and composite samples pass the prescribed tests. 



APPENDIX A 

[Table U Item (nii) ] 
TEST FOR mOROAMIG ACaOTt 

A-1. REAGENT 

A-1.1 Mathyl Ovaag* lMHc»t«r — Dissolve I g of inetliyl<Mr*nge in 000 

litre of distilled water. 



*Method« of MmpUag of pMroleum aod iu producti. 

6 



15:408-1981 

A-2. PROCEDURE 

A-2*l Weigh 50 g of the material, accurately to the nearest 1 g, into a 
separating funnel. Neutralize 100 ml of water, using methyl orange 
indicator. Heat this neutralized water to 70^C and then add it to the 
material in the funnel. Extract the mixture thoroughly by shaking. 
AlloW to stand for the oil and aqueous layer to separate. 

A-2.1.1 The material shall be taken to have passed the test if the 
aqueous layer does not show acid reaction to methyl orange indicator. 



APPENDIX B 

[Table \,Item(i\)] 
TEST FOR RESISTANCE TO BREAKDOWN 

B-1. PROCEDURE 

B-1.1 Mould 10 g of the material into the form of a cone on a small clock 
glass and maintain at 75°C for one hour and then examine. 

B-1.1.1 The material shall be taken to have passed the test if there is 
no separation of oil or other visible sign of breakdown.
